name: Cafe Onion Anguk
summary: A restored hanok turned bakery café: floor cushions, tiled courtyard and the snow-capped pandoro that made Onion famous
description: Onion Anguk sits in a restored hanok a few steps from Anguk Station Exit 3, with seating on wooden maru floors around a tiled courtyard. The bakery counter is the draw: the powdered-sugar pandoro, the onion-basil bagel and seasonal pastries, alongside a proper La Marzocco espresso bar. On Naver it has 10,000+ visitor reviews, and reviewers note that about half the guests are international visitors. Early-week mornings (07:00 opening Mon–Wed) are the best way to get a courtyard seat.
highlights: Pandoro (6,000원) under a mountain of powdered sugar
Courtyard seating on the hanok maru
tips: Naver lists 07:00 opening Mon–Wed and 09:00 on Sundays and 24–26 Sep — arrive before 10:00 to get floor seating for 5 together.
Pastries sell out by late afternoon; a Naver reviewer found almost no bread left after 17:00.
Decaf swap is free, per recent Naver reviews.
Pair with Changdeokgung or Bukchon — it is 3 minutes from Anguk Exit 3.

tripadvisor.rank: #17 of 2,120 Coffee & Tea Spots in Seoul

reviews.text: Nice Hanok surroundings. Picture friendly.
reviews.author: Peterson J

reviews.text: Visitors say the hanok atmosphere makes it easy to talk and linger, and one regular calls the coffee and bakery good value for the quality.
A weekday 1 pm visitor waited under 5 minutes behind three groups; they recommend ordering the onion basil bagel.

name: London Bagel Museum Anguk
summary: Seoul's most famous bagel shop: London-deli interiors, 20+ chewy bagels and queues that need the CatchTable remote waitlist
description: The original London Bagel Museum is a two-storey brick-and-wood space in Bukchon styled like an old London deli, with royal portraits, Union Jacks and baskets of bagels stacked to the ceiling. The chewy bagels start at 3,800원 (plain) and most flavours are 4,700원; the spring-onion cream cheese bagel and the Jambon butter sandwich bagel are the classics. Naver visitors rate it 4.21 with 9,000+ reviews and mostly praise the bread and the photogenic interior. TripAdvisor reviewers love the bagels but warn about long waits.
highlights: Brick Lane bagel (sesame, cream cheese & honey)
tips: Register on the CatchTable app waitlist before you arrive and explore Bukchon while you wait — weekend waits can run 1–3 hours.
Takeaway queue is separate and much faster than eating in.
Also branches at Dosan (Gangnam) and Jamsil if Anguk is too busy.
Weekday opening (07:00) is the quietest time.

reviews.text: After several failed attempts, a visitor got in quickly on a weekday and praised the cheese-honey bagel, friendly staff and the "abroad" feel of the room.
Most-voted praise from Naver visitors: delicious bread (7,266), special menu (3,301), stylish interior (2,671).

chuseok.note: The shop's Naver listing says it opens as normal on public holidays (07:00–18:00 daily); no Chuseok-specific 2026 notice found — expect heavy holiday crowds.

name: Artist Bakery
summary: Salt-butter bread specialists from the London Bagel Museum team — 20+ shiopan flavours next to Anguk Station Exit 1
description: Artist Bakery is the salt-bread (소금빵) sibling of London Bagel Museum, right beside Anguk Station Exit 1 and the Seoul Museum of Craft Art. The counter holds more than twenty versions of shiopan, from the plain 'soft' and 'hard' (3,800원) to truffle, pretzel, basil pesto and cheese-honey (up to 4,900원). Naver visitors rate it 4.37 across nearly 4,000 reviews. Regulars note that eat-in still queues, but takeaway via CatchTable is now almost instant.
tips: Book takeaway through CatchTable — recent reviewers found almost no wait for takeout even when the eat-in queue was long.
Buy a mixed box and eat it at the Seoul Museum of Craft Art plaza next door.
Mornings have the full range; popular flavours sell out.

name: Osulloc Tea House Bukchon
summary: Jeju green-tea maker's three-storey Bukchon flagship: matcha bingsu, tea tastings and terraces over hanok roofs
description: Osulloc, the Jeju tea brand, runs this three-storey tea house on Bukchon-ro: a tea shop with free tastings on the ground floor and lounges above with terraces looking across hanok rooftops. The Bukchon-only roasted green tea and the Hallasan matcha bingsu (18,000원) are the signatures, and a seated tea course (39,000원) suits parents who want a proper tea ceremony. Naver visitors give it 4.76 — one of the highest scores in this guide — praising the tea and the garden-like terraces.
tips: Taste teas for free on the ground floor before choosing what to buy as gifts.
Go up to the 2nd/3rd floor terraces for the hanok-roof view; seats turn over quickly on weekdays.
No parking nearby — walk 7 min from Anguk Exit 2.

reviews.text: Visitors single out the roasted green tea sold only at this branch and the gift shop for tea sets; one family found the matcha a little divisive but loved the bingsu.
Reviewers describe different moods on the 2nd and 3rd floors and a garden-like setting that feels healing, despite many tourists.

name: Cafe Layered Anguk
summary: English tea-room fantasy in a yellow hanok-roofed house: warm scones, clotted cream and pastel layer cakes
description: Layered's original branch is a yellow house with a hanok roof two minutes from Anguk Exit 2, fitted out like an English country tea room. Scones are the specialty — the signature scone is 4,700원 and flavours like Earl Grey and strawberry are 5,500원 — with mini layer cakes such as Victoria and red velvet. TripAdvisor rates it 4.1 over 50 reviews, and Naver visitors mostly praise the bread and desserts.
tips: Staff seat you by party size; weekday mornings (08:00 opening) are easiest for 5.
Tables fill constantly — if full, scones travel well for a picnic at Changdeokgung.

name: Suyeon Sanbang
summary: Tea in novelist Lee Tae-jun's 1930s hanok home in Seongbuk-dong — jujube tea and pumpkin bingsu in a secret garden
description: Suyeon Sanbang is the former house of short-story writer Sangheo Lee Tae-jun, who lived here from 1933 to 1946; it is now a tea house in the hills of Seongbuk-dong. Guests sit on the maru or in the small garden with jujube ssanghwa tea (15,500원) or the famous pumpkin bingsu and red-bean porridge. Naver reviewers call it especially atmospheric on rainy days; they also note it is small, the chairs are not built for long stays and prices are high.
highlights: Garden seating by the old house
tips: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays; closes at 17:50 on weekdays, 19:50 on weekends.
No subway nearby: take Line 4 to Hansung Univ. then bus 1111/2112 to the 이태준가옥 stop, or a taxi (~40 min from home).
Small rooms — a group of 5 may be split; weekday early afternoon is calmest.
Pair with Gilsangsa temple (10 min walk) for a quiet half-day.

reviews.text: Reviewers describe a small but charming reformed hanok where you look at the old house's back garden over tea; calm and atmospheric, though not cheap.
A rainy-day visitor loved the mood and the not-too-sweet homemade red beans, but found the chairs uncomfortable for a long stay.

name: Namusairo Coffee
summary: A long-respected Seoul specialty roaster, pouring monthly single origins in a hanok by Gyeongbokgung
description: Namusairo ('between the trees') is a respected Seoul specialty roaster that moved into a restored hanok with a tiny garden in Naeja-dong, four minutes from Gyeongbokgung Station. Beans rotate monthly and the baristas explain each origin; the espresso and filter coffee are the reason to go, with an amaretto latte and specialty tiramisu for non-purists. TripAdvisor rates it 4.4, and on Naver 'great coffee' is by far the most-voted praise.
highlights: Rain dripping from the hanok eaves
tips: Opens 07:30 — a perfect first stop before Gyeongbokgung gates open.
The coffee of the month is cheaper than the rest of the brew list; beans for home can be bought until 21:00.
Rooms are split across the hanok; 5 people usually fit in the back room.

name: Hakrim Dabang
summary: Seoul’s oldest surviving dabang (1956): creaky stairs, classical LPs, Vienna coffee and famous cream-cheese cake
description: Up a narrow staircase opposite Marronnier Park, Hakrim has served students and writers of Daehangno since 1956 and appeared in the drama 'My Love from the Star'. Dark wood booths, a wall of LP records and classical music set the mood. The house cream-cheese cake and Vienna coffee (6,500원 each) are what everyone orders. TripAdvisor rates it 4.7, and Naver regulars praise the coffee and the old-Seoul interior.
tips: Closed 24–25 Sep for Chuseok; reopens 26 Sep.
Take the 2nd-floor stairs next to Jongno Pharmacy, 1 min from Hyehwa Exit 3.
Open until 23:00 — great after a Daehangno show.
Booths are small; a party of 5 may need two tables side by side.

name: Nudake Tea House Seongsu
summary: Gentle Monster's dessert label in a sculptural Seongsu tea lounge — plates that look like art objects
description: Nudake is the dessert brand of eyewear house Gentle Monster, known for pastries that look like sculptures. Its Seongsu tea house, one of the brand's newest spaces, sits above a gift shop in a vast, gallery-like building on Ttukseom-ro: you browse the ground floor, then climb to a hushed tea lounge. The menu is conceptual — the Peak Small cake, the 155MM, a nine-piece petits fours collection (34,000원) — paired with house teas. Naver visitors (4.71) love the concept and design; several say it is pricey and 'not about value'.
highlights: Tea pairings in the upper lounge
tips: Tea lounge 12:00–21:00 (last order 20:15); the gift shop opens at 11:00.
Popular desserts sell out — go at noon opening.
Budget ~25,000–35,000원 per person; share plates across the family.
13 min walk from Seongsu Stn Exit 3; combine with Seoul Forest.

reviews.text: One reviewer said it felt like being invited to a secret gathering: whisky-scented tea and chocolate desserts, with popular items selling out early.
Another called it pricey with "no value for money", but the molecular-gastronomy style desserts and the walk up through the building were a unique experience.

summary: The café that launched Seongsu: a raw 1970s factory with the famous pandoro and plenty of room for groups
description: Onion Seongsu occupies a 1970s factory-era building left deliberately raw, with exposed brick, concrete and peeling paint. It is large enough to seat a family together, and the bakery (pandoro, salt bread, seasonal pastries) is the same quality as the Anguk hanok branch. TripAdvisor rates it 4.2 over 91 reviews; Naver reviewers mention many international visitors and the unique abandoned-factory feel.
tips: Naver lists 08:00 opening Mon–Wed and 09:00 on Sundays and 24–26 Sep — the early hours are quiet.
Bigger than Onion Anguk: the best Onion branch for a group of 5.
No parking; 5 min from Seongsu Exit 2.

name: Daelim Changgo Gallery
summary: A cavernous old warehouse turned gallery café — trees, sculptures and firewood-lined walls in Seongsu
description: Daelim Changgo is the converted warehouse that defined Seongsu's factory-café style: soaring ceilings, big installations and paintings, and long timber tables with room for any group. It serves coffee (a Geisha signature), panettone, organic strawberry milk and craft beer. TripAdvisor rates it 4.2 over 41 reviews and some say food is 'just okay and a bit pricey'; Naver visitors vote most for coffee, the interior and the spacious hall.
highlights: Art installations under the old warehouse roof
tips: Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep); open 24 and 26.
Huge space — easiest spot in Seongsu to sit 5 people together.
Toilets are few for the size; expect a short line.
5 min from Seongsu Stn Exit 3.

name: Coffee Hanyakbang
summary: A hand-roasted coffee den styled like an old herbal pharmacy, hidden in an Euljiro alley
description: Coffee Hanyakbang ('coffee herbal pharmacy') hides down a narrow alley near Euljiro 3-ga Station, dressed in antique cabinets, old radios and jazz on the turntable. Coffee is roasted over direct flame and brewed by hand; the signature sujeonggwa-in-gabe (cinnamon-ginger punch coffee, 7,000원) is unique. TripAdvisor rates it 4.5 over 33 reviews (one reviewer calls it their go-to espresso in Korea).
tips: Open on all Chuseok days with shorter holiday hours (11:00–20:00).
Look for the tiny alley off Samil-daero 12-gil; follow the signs from Euljiro 3-ga Exit 1.
Rooms are small — split between the 1st and 2nd floor if you are 5.
The famous Hyeminbang bakery opposite has closed, per a September 2026 review.

name: Starbucks Gyeongdong 1960
summary: A 1960s cinema inside Gyeongdong Market reborn as Starbucks — tiered theatre seating and market-only drinks
description: On the 3rd–4th floors above Gyeongdong Market, the former 1960s Gyeongdong Theatre was restored as a Starbucks that keeps the stepped auditorium as seating. Naver reviewers note it was picked among the Korea Tourism Organization × Starbucks top-10 special stores, and it sells store-only drinks such as a honey-hotteok latte. summary: A Starbucks floating on the Han River at Jamwon — wall-to-wall water views, 15 minutes from home by taxi
description: Seoul Wave Art Center is a floating culture complex moored at Jamwon Hangang Park in Seocho-gu, and its Starbucks puts glass walls right on the water, facing the Han River and the northern skyline. It works like any Starbucks (app ordering, coupons), with standard prices. Naver visitors vote 'great view' most, and reviewers praise both daytime and night views; one notes you can walk on to Banpo Bridge for the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain.
tips: Open 07:00–22:00 on 24–27 Sep (posted on Naver) — a reliable open spot on Chuseok day.
Jamwon Stn Exit 3/4 is a 15-min walk; bus 143/345/4318 to 잠원한신아파트 then 5 min, or a short taxi from home.
More window seats were added recently, per Naver reviews.
Check the Banpo Bridge fountain schedule and walk there after sunset.

reviews.text: A reviewer calls it the best river-view spot on the Han: great by day, beautiful at night, and a short walk to the Banpo Bridge fountain show.
A visitor who spilled a drink was given a free remake with a smile — staff described as very kind.

hours.note: Naver lists 07:00–22:00 for 24–27 Sep and 08:30–22:00 for 28–29 Sep.

name: Sulbing Gangnam Station
summary: Korea’s best-known bingsu chain: fluffy milk-snow bingsu to share, open through Chuseok at Gangnam Station
description: Sulbing popularised the fluffy 'snow' milk bingsu, starting with the injeolmi (roasted soybean & rice cake) bingsu, and a single bowl easily serves two or three people. This Gangnam Station branch is upstairs, behind the SPAO building, and is a practical, inexpensive dessert stop near home. Naver visitors vote desserts first and 214 call it good value.
tips: Open 11:30–22:00 on all Chuseok days (posted on Naver).
Order 2 bowls for 5 people.
Gangnam Stn Exit 11 (5 min) — 2 stops from Seocho/Gyodae on Line 2.
Other branches across Seoul if you crave bingsu elsewhere.

name: Taegeukdang
summary: Seoul’s oldest bakery (1946): retro hall, butter bread and the legendary milk monaka ice cream
description: Taegeukdang has baked in Jangchung-dong since 1946 and is widely called Seoul's oldest surviving bakery; the hall keeps its retro signage and old-Seoul feel. Order the milk monaka ice-cream sandwich (3,300원), butter bread (3,100원) and 'sarada' salad bread, which regulars say first-timers must try. Naver visitors (22,000+ reviews) vote 'bread is delicious' above all; TripAdvisor is more mixed at 3.7 over 55 reviews.
tips: Open every day of Chuseok; 25 Sep closes early at 19:00 (posted on Naver).
Right at Dongguk Univ. Stn Exit 2 (Line 3 direct from Nambu Bus Terminal, no transfer).
Pair with Jangchung-dong jokbal street or the Namsan walk.
Traditional gift boxes (from 22,000원) make easy souvenirs.

A first-time visitor loved the cream-filled choux bread and fresh-cream bread, overflowing with filling.

name: Cafe Dolce Some Sevit
summary: Coffee inside the futuristic Some Sevit floating islands by Banpo Bridge — river views, open through Chuseok
description: Some Sevit (Sebitseom) is a trio of glassy floating islands moored beside Banpo Bridge in Seocho-gu, lit in changing colours at night. Cafe Dolce sits inside, with river-facing seating and inexpensive drinks such as a 'Sevit Hangang' lemonade (7,500원) and americano (4,800원). Naver visitors vote coffee and 'great view' highest. It is the closest Han River café to home.
highlights: River-view seats inside the floating islands
Banpo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain nearby
tips: Open 10:30–22:00 on 24–26 Sep (posted on Naver); weekday hours 11:00–21:00.
About 18 min walk from Express Bus Terminal Stn — a taxi from home is ~10 min.
Time it with the Banpo Bridge fountain show after dark (check the season schedule).

reviews.text: Naver visitors vote coffee (519) and view (438) highest, followed by drinks and desserts.
Naver's review highlight describes a relaxed place for a cup of coffee.

name: Urban Plant Hangang Bridge
summary: A café perched on Hangang Bridge itself — Einspänner and pasta with the river flowing on both sides
description: Urban Plant occupies the observation-café building on the south end of Hangang Bridge, so you sit above the water with the river and Nodeul Island around you. Coffee (americano 5,000원, Einspänner 7,500원) and brunch plates such as perilla-pesto pasta (17,600원) make it a light-meal stop too. It scores 4.91 across 1,800+ Naver visitor reviews, with the interior, view and photo-friendliness most praised.
tips: Open daily 10:00–22:00 per Naver; no Chuseok notice.
Easiest by bus to the "한강대교전망카페" stop (right outside) or by taxi; Nodeul Stn (Line 9) is ~17 min on foot.
Go before sunset for window seats.
Combine with Nodeul Island (music & park) next door.

reviews.text: Naver visitors vote interior (1,293), view (1,156) and coffee (917) highest; 812 say it is great for photos.
Naver's review highlight: an Einspänner paired with the Han River view.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok notice found. Regular hours suggest open on 24 & 26 Sep; Chuseok day (25 Sep) unconfirmed — call ahead.

name: Whitelier Banpo
summary: A Banpo neighbourhood bakery famous for its pillowy premium milk loaf and house jams — five minutes from Banpo Station
description: Whitelier's original shop sits in the Banpo Shopping Center arcade, reached through the underground passage from Banpo Station (Line 7) and the GOTO Mall. It is known for one thing above all: the premium 'saeng-sikppang' milk loaf (11,000원 full, 6,000원 half), eaten plain or with house jams like strawberry-butter and Earl Grey milk (8,000–9,000원). Naver visitors (4.49 across 2,400+ reviews) vote 'the bread is delicious' overwhelmingly, and a loaf makes an easy breakfast for five back at home.
tips: Closed 25–26 Sep for Chuseok (posted on Naver); open 24 Sep 10:00–21:00.
Use Banpo Stn underground passage exit G14 (~30 m); from home it is about 10 min by taxi or Line 3→7 via Express Bus Terminal.
Buy a loaf plus one jam for a family breakfast — mostly takeaway.

reviews.text: Naver visitors vote "bread is delicious" (1,545) far above everything else, followed by friendly staff (303) and special menu (262).
